{{Short description|Principal fiber bundle}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''circle bundle''' is a [[fiber bundle]] where the fiber is the [[circle]] <math>S^1</math>.

Oriented circle bundles are also known as [[principal bundle|principal ''U''(1)-bundles]], or equivalently, as principal ''SO''(2)-bundles. In [[physics]], circle bundles are the natural geometric setting for [[electromagnetism]]. A circle bundle is a special case of a [[sphere bundle]].

==As 3-manifolds==
Circle bundles over [[surface (topology)|surface]]s are an important example of [[3-manifold]]s.  A more general class of 3-manifolds is [[Seifert fiber space]]s, which may be viewed as a kind of "singular" circle bundle, or as a circle bundle over a two-dimensional [[orbifold]].

==Relationship to electrodynamics==
The [[Maxwell equation]]s correspond to an [[electromagnetic field]] represented by a [[2-form]] ''F'', with <math>\pi^{\!*}F</math> being [[cohomologous]] to zero, i.e. [[Closed and exact differential forms|exact]]. In particular, there always exists a [[1-form]] ''A'', the [[electromagnetic four-potential]], (equivalently, the [[affine connection]]) such that

:<math> \pi^{*}F = dA.</math>

Given a circle bundle ''P'' over ''M'' and its projection

:<math>\pi:P\to M</math>

one has the [[homomorphism]]

:<math>\pi^*:H^2(M,\mathbb{Z}) \to H^2(P,\mathbb{Z})</math>

where <math>\pi^{*}</math> is the [[pullback]]. Each homomorphism corresponds to a [[Dirac monopole]]; the integer [[cohomology group]]s correspond to the quantization of the [[electric charge]].  The [[Aharonov–Bohm effect]] can be understood as the [[holonomy]] of the connection on the associated line bundle describing the electron wave-function. In essence, the Aharonov–Bohm effect is not a quantum-mechanical effect (contrary to popular belief), as no quantization is involved or required in the construction of the fiber bundles or connections.

==Examples==
* The [[Hopf fibration]] is an example of a non-trivial circle bundle. <!-- This should be spelled out explicitly using the quotient of SU(2) by U(1) constructing the homogeneous space S^2 -->
* The unit tangent bundle of a surface is another example of a circle bundle.
* The unit tangent bundle of a non-orientable surface is a circle bundle that is not a principal <math>U(1)</math> bundle.  Only orientable surfaces have principal unit tangent bundles.
* Another method for constructing circle bundles is using a complex line bundle <math>L \to X</math> and taking the associated sphere (circle in this case) bundle. Since this bundle has an orientation induced from <math>L</math> we have that it is a principal <math>U(1)</math>-bundle.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://mathoverflow.net/q/144092| title=Is every orientable circle bundle principal? - MathOverflow}}</ref> Moreover, the characteristic classes from Chern-Weil theory of the <math>U(1)</math>-bundle agree with the characteristic classes of <math>L</math>.
* For example, consider the analytification <math>X</math> a complex plane curve <math> \text{Proj}\left( \frac{\Complex[x,y,z]}{x^n + y^n + z^n} \right)</math>. Since <math>H^2(X) = \mathbb{Z} = H^2(\mathbb{CP}^2)</math> and the characteristic classes pull back non-trivially, we have that the line bundle associated to the sheaf <math>\mathcal{O}_X(a) = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(a)\otimes \mathcal{O}_X</math> has Chern class <math>c_1 = a \in H^2(X)</math>.

==Classification==
The [[isomorphism class]]es of principal <math>U(1)</math>-bundles over a manifold ''M'' are in one-to-one correspondence with the [[homotopy class]]es of maps <math>M \to BU(1)</math>, where <math>BU(1)</math> is called the [[Classifying space for U(n)|classifying space for U(1)]]. Note that <math>BU(1)= \mathbb{C}P^\infty</math> is the infinite-dimensional [[complex projective space]], and that it is an example of the [[Eilenberg–Maclane space]] <math>K(\mathbb{Z},2).</math> Such bundles are classified by an element of the second [[integral cohomology group]] <math>H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})</math> of ''M'', since 
:<math>[M,BU(1)] \equiv [M,\mathbb CP^\infty] \equiv H^2(M)</math>.
This isomorphism is realized by the [[Euler class]]; equivalently, it is the first [[Chern class]] of a smooth complex [[line bundle]] (essentially because a circle is homotopically equivalent to <math>\mathbb{C}^*</math>, the complex plane with the origin removed; and so a complex line bundle with the zero section removed is homotopically equivalent to a circle bundle.)

A circle bundle is a principal <math>U(1)</math> bundle if and only if the associated map <math>M \to B\mathbb Z_2</math> is null-homotopic, which is true if and only if the bundle is fibrewise orientable. Thus, for the more general case, where the circle bundle over ''M'' might not be orientable, the isomorphism classes are in one-to-one correspondence with the [[homotopy class]]es of maps <math>M \to BO_2</math>. This follows from the extension of groups, <math>SO_2 \to O_2 \to \mathbb Z_2</math>, where <math>SO_2 \equiv U(1)</math>.

===Deligne complexes===
{{main|Deligne cohomology}}
The above classification only applies to circle bundles in general; the corresponding classification for smooth circle bundles, or, say, the circle bundles with an [[affine connection]] requires a more complex cohomology theory. Results include that the smooth circle bundles are classified by the second Deligne cohomology <math>H_D^2(M, \mathbb{Z})</math>; circle bundles with an affine connection are classified by <math>H_D^2(M, \mathbb{Z}(2))</math> while <math>H_D^3(M, \mathbb{Z})</math> classifies line bundle [[gerbe]]s.
